prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Customer Onboarding Field Validation Rules (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Field" · longest unbreakable word 126px · one-line width 126px
  col 2: header "Pattern" · longest unbreakable word 114px · one-line width 1074px
  col 3: header "Example valid" · longest unbreakable word 167px · one-line width 264px
  col 4: header "Error message" · longest unbreakable word 157px · one-line width 700px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A developer/QA reference sheet: for each onboarding form field it gives the validation regex, a valid sample, and the message shown on failure — a lookup table read row by row while implementing or testing one field.","reading":"Readers arrive knowing the field name (or scan the Field column as an index), then move right to the pattern, check it against the example, and read the error copy. Comparison happens within a row, not down a column, so each row must read as a single unit and the Field column must stay a stable anchor; the regex is the densest, most consulted content and the error text is the only true prose.","groups":["col 1 Field is the row key and stands alone — it is the lookup handle and must remain visually distinct and unbroken","col 2 Pattern + col 3 Example valid form a spec pair: the rule and a value that satisfies it, read together and verified against each other","col 4 Error message is the outcome/consequence text, the only column of ordinary prose, and can wrap freely without losing meaning"],"keep_intact":["field identifiers such as account_email, postal_code_us, currency_amount, eu_vat_id (no mid-word breaks)","regex anchors and atoms: ^, $, \\d{7,14}, [A-Za-z0-9._!...], (?:-\\d{4})? — break only at |, (, [, { boundaries, never inside a character class or quantifier","example values such as an email address or 2024-01-15 (break at @ or - at worst)"],"may_wrap":["error-message sentences — natural prose, wraps at word spaces with no loss","long regex alternation/branch sequences — wrap between groups, not inside them","header labels 'Example valid' and 'Error message' over two lines"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [147, 560, 188, 190] · table 1086×826px · row heights [36, 106, 153, 83, 83, 129, 129, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 726px
Design r2B: widths [147, 470, 215, 195] · table 1028×779px · row heights [36, 106, 129, 83, 83, 129, 129, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 668px
Design r2C: widths [147, 430, 188, 180] · table 946×849px · row heights [36, 106, 153, 106, 83, 129, 129, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 586px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r2A","good":"The regex column is the most readable of the three: at 560px the long account_email rule breaks at group boundaries (`(?:\\.[A-Za-z0-9])?` starts a new line) into 4 clean fragments, and the Field column sits exactly at its 147px no-split minimum so identifiers stay whole.","problems":"Worst overflow of the three (1086px, 726px past the box), so Example valid and Error message are both entirely off-screen at 360px and no row can be read as a unit — the reader sees a field name and a wall of regex and nothing else. Worse, it buys nothing: the tallest cell is still 6 lines, one line *taller* than r2B which is 58px narrower. Row 4 (effective_date) is 153px tall although its regex fits on one line at this width.","cause":"Pattern is given 560px — about 90px past the point where the regex stops being the binding constraint. Once a row's height is set by the Error/Example columns (190/188, near their floors), extra pattern width converts 1:1 into scroll cost and zero legibility gain. The width budget is being spent on the column that already fits."},{"design":"r2B","good":"The strongest of the three: shortest table (779px) and the lowest tallest-cell (5 lines), because 470px is right at the threshold where most patterns fall into 2–3 structure-respecting lines, and the prose columns at 215/195 are generous enough to keep error copy to 4 lines. No mid-word splits anywhere.","problems":"Still 668px of overflow, so the two right-hand columns — the ones that tell you whether the rule works and what the user sees when it doesn't — are invisible on arrival. Pattern stays at 465 — right at the threshold where the long regex breaks at group boundaries — so total falls from 1028 to 1005 while the tallest row should drop by a line. Example at its 188 floor, error at 185 just above its 178 floor. Trades ~1 extra pattern line on 3 rows for 128px less scrolling."},{"name":"phone-min","widths":[147,300,188,178],"change":"Tests the other end of the spectrum, which none of the current designs explore: total 813px, only 453px past the box, so one short swipe brings the whole row — field, pattern, example, error — into view together and the row finally reads as a unit. Prose columns at their exact floors (188/178) so no words split; the pattern accepts 3–5 chopped lines, but it is already unreadable in one glance at any of these widths, and its breaks still fall at | ( [ { boundaries. If a phone reader must scroll anyway, pay in vertical height (cheap) rather than horizontal distance (expensive)."}]}
